# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview
Both billing systems (legacy "Old Billing" and new "New Billing") will run concurrently throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches by moving their account-of-record and active billing operations (invoicing, payment processing, subscription changes) to the new system, while the old system remains live, read-accessible, and capable of processing fallback transactions until the final phase's stabilization window has passed.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — 800 users)

**Entry Criterion:** New billing system has passed full parallel-run reconciliation testing against the old system for 30 consecutive days with zero unresolved discrepancies in invoice totals, tax calculation, and payment posting; rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end in staging.

**Scope:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk customers (no active disputes, month-to-month plans, no enterprise contracts).

**Activities:** Migrate accounts, run daily dual-invoice comparison (old system generates invoice in shadow mode, compared against new system's live invoice), manual review of every transaction.

**Exit Criterion:** 800 users migrated with invoice/payment accuracy ≥ 99.9%, no P1/P2 incidents open, support ticket volume from pilot cohort within 1.5x baseline.

---

## Phase 2: Expanded Rollout (28% of users — 11,200 users, cumulative 30%)

**Entry Criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by Billing Engineering Lead and Customer Support Lead; automated reconciliation dashboard live (replacing manual review); at least 2 weeks elapsed post-Phase 1 with no reopened incidents.

**Scope:** Broadened segment including mid-tier customers across multiple geographies and plan types, still excluding enterprise/custom-contract accounts.

**Activities:** Batch migrations in waves of ~2,000 users every 3–4 days, automated daily reconciliation, monitoring of payment failure rates and support escalations per wave before proceeding to next wave.

**Exit Criterion:** Cumulative payment failure rate ≤ 0.5% above pre-migration baseline; billing support ticket volume ≤ 1.3x baseline sustained for 2 weeks; no unresolved P1 incidents.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (70% of users — 28,000 users, cumulative 100%)

**Entry Criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; finance has reconciled Phase 1+2 revenue recognition against old system with no material variance; enterprise/custom-contract account migration runbook separately reviewed and approved by Legal and Finance (these accounts migrate last within this phase due to contractual complexity).

**Scope:** All remaining users, including enterprise and custom-contract accounts (migrated in the final sub-batch of this phase).

**Activities:** Migrate remaining users in waves of ~5,000–7,000, prioritizing standard accounts first and enterprise accounts last; maintain old system in full standby/fallback mode for all migrated users.

**Exit Criterion:** 100% of users migrated; reconciliation accuracy ≥ 99.9% sustained for 30 days; zero open P1 incidents.

**Post-Phase 3 (separate phase, not part of final migration batch):** Old billing system moves to read-only archival mode no earlier than 60 days after Phase 3 exit criteria are met, followed by formal decommissioning only after finance archival and audit sign-off. Decommissioning is explicitly scheduled as its own phase, distinct from the final user-migration batch.

---

## Risks

RISK: Payment processing failures spike during cutover due to tokenization mismatches between old and new payment gateways | Run parallel tokenization validation for each batch 48 hours before cutover and auto-rollback any account with failed token validation | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Revenue recognition discrepancies between old and new systems cause financial reporting errors | Daily automated reconciliation reports reviewed by Finance with mandatory sign-off before each subsequent wave | Finance Controller
RISK: Customer support volume overwhelms team due to billing confusion or duplicate charges | Pre-scale support staffing per phase using projected ticket volume models and maintain a dedicated migration escalation queue | Customer Support Director
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated incorrectly, causing contractual breach | Require Legal and Account Management sign-off on each enterprise account's migration mapping before inclusion in any batch | Enterprise Accounts Manager
RISK: Data corruption or loss during account data transfer between systems | Maintain immutable snapshots of old system data pre-migration and run automated field-level validation post-migration for every account | Data Engineering Lead

---

## Halt Metric

If the **payment failure rate for any migration wave exceeds 2% above the pre-migration baseline**, measured over a rolling 24-hour window, the rollout is immediately halted, no further batches are migrated, and the incident response team triages before any subsequent wave proceeds.

PHASES: 3
